findings.title: [P2] Reject non-finite timeout values instead of returning them
findings.body: The guard only throws when `Number.isFinite(timeout)` is true, so `NaN` and `±Infinity` short-circuit past validation and are returned. Verified by direct evaluation of the head version: `"abc"` and `"Infinity"` now return `NaN`/`Infinity` instead of throwing `"invalid timeout"` as before (`parseInt` + `isSafeInteger` rejected them), and `"10ms"` returns `NaN` where the old code returned `10`. This breaks the parser's positive-safe-integer contract and the PR's stated intent to preserve contracts. Since `Number.isSafeInteger` already rejects every non-finite value, the `Number.isFinite` conjunct should be removed (or the check inverted) so non-finite values throw again.
